## Goal

Make the administration area safe to expose: a verified owner account exists before anything is public, and a second factor is required to use it.

## Context

Any authenticated user of the administration collection has full rights over the whole admin area, including customer and accounting records. After the documented initialisation the administrator table is empty, and the framework offers its own first-user registration. The deployment procedure does not yet make an existing, verified administrator a precondition for serving public traffic. Details are in the owner's private tracker.

## Scope

- A boot-time condition that refuses to serve production traffic unless a verified administrator exists, covering a fresh install, a restore from backup and the state after the last administrator is removed.
- A private initialisation step in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` for creating the owner account before the site is reachable.
- A proposal for the second factor, with the trade-offs of doing it in the application versus at an identity gateway in front of it, as a decision entry for the owner. Implement the option the owner picks.
- `docs/LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md` updated to match.

## Out of scope

- Changing customer authentication (SC-021).
- Changing access rules of individual collections.
- Buying a paid identity service without owner approval.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh install cannot serve public traffic without an administrator, proven by a test.
- [ ] The owner account creation procedure has been followed once on staging and recorded.
- [ ] The second factor is required on every administrator entry point, including recovery, verified by hand on staging.
- [ ] Independent review approves.

## Required tests

- Tests for the boot condition.
- A manual staging check of administrator sign-in and recovery, recorded on the issue.
- All standard checks.

## Dependencies

- SC-003

## Priority

P1 · Phase A
